title: Combining Google Earth Historical Imagery and UAV Photogrammetry for Urban Development Analysis
author: Iheaturu, Okolie, et al.

steps.title: Project historical imagery
steps.instruction: Use ArcMap 10.8 to re‑project the Google Earth historical raster from Geographic WGS84 to the orthomosaic coordinate system (UTM Zone 32 N, Minna).

substeps.instruction: Open ArcToolbox → Data Management Tools → Projections and Transformations → Raster → Project Raster.
In the Project Raster dialog, browse to select the input raster (the GE historical image in WGS84).
Browse to choose an output folder and name for the projected raster.
Set the output coordinate system to UTM Zone 32 N (Minna) and click OK to create the projected raster.

steps.title: Georeference projected raster
steps.instruction: Align the projected historical image with the orthomosaic by adding control points derived from common visible features.

substeps.instruction: Load both the projected raster and the orthomosaic into ArcMap and visualise them side‑by‑side.
Identify at least several clearly matching features (e.g., building corners, road intersections) in both images.
Manually record the coordinates of each feature on the orthomosaic.
Open the Georeferencing toolbar, choose “Add Control Points”, and enter the recorded orthomosaic coordinates for the corresponding points on the projected raster.
After adding sufficient control points, apply the transformation to complete georeferencing.

steps.title: Digitise urban features
steps.instruction: Create shapefiles for building footprints, plots, and roads and digitise them from the georeferenced images.

substeps.instruction: Create a working folder on the C: drive to store all outputs.

In ArcCatalog, right‑click the working folder → New → Shapefile. Name the file (e.g., Building_footprints), set Feature Type to Polygon, and assign Spatial Reference UTM Zone 32 N (Minna). Repeat for plots (polygon) and roads (line).
In ArcMap, click the Editor menu and select “Start Editing”.
Open the “Create Features” window, select a shapefile (e.g., Building_footprints), and digitise the feature by adding vertices along its boundary.
Save edits, stop editing, and repeat the digitising process for each remaining feature class (plots, roads).

steps.title: Create and export map layout
steps.instruction: Symbolise the shapefiles, compose a map layout, add map elements, and export the final map as a high‑resolution JPEG.

substeps.instruction: Apply appropriate symbology to each shapefile (e.g., fill colour for buildings, line style for roads).
Switch to Layout View via View → Layout View.
Open File → Page and Print Setup, set page size to A4 and orientation to Landscape, then click OK.
Use the Insert menu to add a Title, Legend, North Arrow, Scale Bar, and Scale Text to the layout.
Add a measured grid: View → Data Frame Properties → Grid → New Grid → Measured Grid; set desired appearance, intervals, axes, and labels, then finish.
Export the map: File → Export Map, specify file name (e.g., GE_Map_2005), choose format JPEG, set resolution to 300 dpi, and click Save.
